title: NMC bars AI-generated patient testimonials, clinical outcomes in medical advertising | India News
source_used: Hindustan Times (text from a news agency feed; agency not named)
key_facts: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has barred doctors and hospitals from using AI to create or circulate fabricated patient experiences, clinical outcomes and endorsements.
The guidelines say AI cannot be used to create synthetic patient testimonials, voices, clinical outcomes or fake endorsements.
Doctors may not call themselves 'best', 'number one', 'most trusted', 'guaranteed cures' or '100% success' unless the claims are verifiable.

Penalties: a warning and ethics training for a first violation; censure and a fine for a second; suspension for three to six months for a third; suspension for six to 12 months for serious violations; removal from the medical register for one to three years for repeated violations.
Doctors may not pay influencers, agencies or platforms for patient referrals, nor offer limited-period discounts or referral gifts that encourage unnecessary consultations.
Doctors may still give factual, non-promotional health education on social media.
quote_evidence: AI cannot be used to create synthetic patient testimonials, voices, clinical outcomes or fake endorsements
The new norms, which were issued by the National Medical Commission on Wednesday and have come into effect immediately
why_it_matters_hint: A national rule for AI-made medical advertising matters to patients who choose care from online promotions.
